_comment: Bundled fallback for the presenter board. ?offline=1 runs the whole narration off this.

model.baseRate: Placeholder — no model call has been made yet.
reasons: Run `npm run model` to replace this with a real forecast.
Then run `npm run snapshot` so the offline board matches.

divergence.label: The room is materially more pessimistic than the model. That gap is the most useful thing on this screen — it marks the assumption worth arguing about.

notes.note: Three separate edge appliances hit KEV in the last eighteen months. The base rate alone gets you most of the way there.
The binding constraint is public attribution, not exploitation. Plenty happens that nobody names.
Two years is a long window and OAIC reporting has been getting more specific, not less.
Everyone is anchoring on exploitation. The question asks for a named Australian victim, and that pairing is genuinely rarer than it feels.
ASD advisories have named sectors before. It only takes one ASX-listed disclosure to resolve this.
Edge devices are where the unpatchable stuff lives. Nobody reboots the VPN concentrator.
Attribution is the hard part. Australian organisations disclose the breach and stay quiet about the vector.
I would take the other side of anything under 90% here.
Vendor disclosure timelines are the rate limiter, and they are slow by design.
Reading the ambiguity rule closely, endpoint agents are excluded and that removes most of what I was thinking of.
Two independent news reports is a low bar. This resolves on a quiet Tuesday and nobody notices.
It has probably already happened and we are waiting on the paperwork.
